title: refuses a cached archive that is not its pinned bytes, and fetches it afresh
why: A cached archive kept without its sha256 checked: a corrupted cache entry would be built from, and shipped.

title: refuses a cached archive that is a link, even to the right bytes
why: A link kept as a cached archive: the saved entry would hold a link to a file outside it, and the next run's copy would point at nothing or at bytes no one checked.

title: fetches nothing for a warm cache, with the host gone
why: A release tarball fetched whether or not the cache held it: a warm run would still depend on ffmpeg.org, which is the outage the cache is for.

title: tries a download again after a failed try, and keeps what the later try fetched
why: One try only: a single reset connection, curl's (35), which curl's own --retry does not retry, would fail the job again.

title: gives up after four tries, and leaves no part of a download behind
why: More tries than the four the workflows' timeouts were sized for: a dead host would hold the job until its timeout, not fail it.

title: gives up after four tries, and leaves no part of a download behind
why: A failed try's part left where it was written: a stale .part in the next try's way, or in a developer's sources folder, where a link of that name would be written through.

title: leaves both keys alone when a pin outside the ffmpeg block moves
why: The built-ffmpeg cache keyed on the whole pins file again: every engine pin would rebuild ffmpeg on every platform and fetch its sources, as before issue 630.

find: listing = "".join(f"{name} {sha}\n" for name, sha in archives)
replace: listing = "".join(f"{name}\n" for name, sha in archives)
title: moves the sources key when an archive’s pinned sha256 does
why: The source cache keyed on the names alone: a new pin of the same file name would restore the old bytes, every run refusing them and fetching, and never saving the new ones.

title: moves the pins hash, and not the sources key, when anything else in the ffmpeg block does
why: The source cache keyed on the whole ffmpeg block: a configure line or a note changing would fetch the same pinned archives from ffmpeg.org again.

title: takes the archives from the source cache and tries a signature again after a failed try
why: The signature fetched once: a single timeout or reset from ffmpeg.org on the .asc would fail the ffmpeg-source job, and with it every ffmpeg job of the run.

title: refuses a download that is not its pinned bytes, without trying again or keeping it
why: A downloaded archive used without its sha256 checked: whatever the host served would be built from, saved to the cache and shipped.

title: refuses an x264 tar that is not its pinned bytes, and keeps none
why: x264's tar used without its sha256 checked: a commit whose archive is not the pinned tar would be built from and saved to the cache.

title: refuses a download that is not its pinned bytes in --sources too, and copies nothing
why: A wrong download left in the sources folder: unpinned bytes where the next run, or a developer, would find them.
